name: AD8022 (ADI dual high-speed, low-noise op-amp)
tagline: ADI's 130 MHz, 2.5 nV/√Hz XFCB bipolar dual; Head-Fi op-amp rollers say it beats NJM4580 in resolution and comes close to an AD797.
technology: Dual voltage-feedback bipolar op-amp on ADI's high-voltage XFCB (complementary bipolar) process. Datasheet title: 'Dual High Speed, Low Noise Op Amp'. High output current, built to stay stable into capacitive loads.

lineage.period: Rev 0 datasheet (date not confirmed) to present; Rev A 9/02, Rev B 5/05, Rev C 8/11
lineage.notes: Single-source ADI part on the XFCB high-voltage bipolar process. No second sources are known.

key_specs.value: +5 V single, or ±2.5 V to ±12 V

reputation.summary: Posters in Head-Fi's 'The Opamp thread' say replacing the NJM4580 with the AD8022 improved resolution and timbre accuracy, and that it sounds close to the AD797ANZ. They describe it as spatial, clear and very transparent ('pure music'), and say it can drive headphones directly. Caveats: it needs careful decoupling or it oscillates, and its high input bias current makes it poor for high-impedance inputs. This is a niche reputation from forum op-amp rolling, not a widely cited audio standard.
typical_uses: op-amp rolling in NJM4580/NE5532 sockets (DACs, portable players, sound cards)
direct headphone drive at modest levels (per forum posters)
low-impedance, low-noise preamp and ADC-driver stages (datasheet design intent)
caveats: 130 MHz bandwidth: needs tight decoupling and short layout, and can oscillate in socket adapters
bipolar input with relatively high input bias current: poor choice behind high-impedance sources or large feedback resistors
SOIC/MSOP only, so it needs a DIP-8 adapter for socket rolling

counterfeit_notes: No documented AD8022 counterfeit reports found in this pass. Low-cost multi-pack marketplace listings (e.g. Amazon 'AD8022ARZ AD8022AR SOP-8') come from unknown sources. Buy from authorized distributors, because remarked parts are common for SOIC audio duals.

Technology now names the XFCB high-voltage complementary bipolar process and voltage-feedback topology.
Added datasheet revisions and dates: Rev 0 (date unknown), Rev A 9/02, Rev B 5/05, Rev C 8/11 (current).
Added PCN 14_0246 (MSOP assembly-site addition, ASE Chungli). It is an assembly change, not a die change.

revision_chain_notes:
Analog Devices AD8022 is the only document. The part is single-source, and no acquirer re-issue or second source was found. Known chain, oldest to newest: Rev 0 (initial release, date still unknown, before 9/02) -> Rev A (9/02) -> Rev B (5/05) -> Rev C (8/11, current; ADI product page content last updated 02/23/2017).

Copies holding each revision:
- Rev 0: none found. This is the missing link, and its date is unconfirmed. The alldatasheet id 48381 copy and the digchip copy (digchip.com/.../041/AD8022.php, with an unusual title 'Dual Low Noise, Low Distortion, High ...') are candidates, but no revision marking is shown.
- Rev A: the University of Chicago EDG copy. The search snippet for edg.uchicago.edu/~bogdan/ADC_QUIET/DOC/parts/AD8022.pdf literally shows 'REV. A Information furnished by Analog Devices...', so its confidence can be raised to high. Its title uses the plural 'Dual High Speed Low Noise Op Amps'.
- Rev B: no copy confirmed. The search engine's AI summary called the datasheet.su copy (pdf2.datasheet.su/international%20rectifier/auir2085s.pdf, already listed, singular title without 'Data Sheet') Rev B, but no page text showed a Rev B marking, so this is unverified and stays low confidence.
- Rev C: analog.com (upper- and lowercase PDF URLs), icbase.com ADI13561611.pdf, manuallib / archive.org 2588286, and RadioLocman di=121365 (.de and .com).

Still missing:
1. A copy of Rev 0 and its release date. The AD8022 appeared around 1999-2000, but this is not confirmed.
2. A confirmed Rev B (5/05) copy.
3. Per-revision change descriptions from the Rev C revision-history table. The search summaries did not show them.
4. A legacy http://www.analog.com/static/imported-files/data_sheets/ URL. None was found, so none is recorded, but a Wayback lookup of that path could yield Rev B.

All 4 searches were used.
